title: Reviewed hiring evidence for an AI/ML portfolio strategy

methodology.selection: Purposive review from 11 accessible employer-controlled Greenhouse feeds. Original selection contains17 AI/ML roles; three adjacent early-career software roles were added from the same captures to examine transition routes.
methodology.unit: One distinct job ID; geography variants were not counted as separate examples of the same selected role.
methodology.notRepresentative: Large technology employers and English-language accessible feeds are overrepresented. The sample does not estimate global skill prevalence, job counts, hiring odds, beginner accessibility or the effect of a portfolio on hiring.
methodology.dateCaution: Feed updated_at is not treated as original publication date. Captures were made6Nov2026UTC; review completed7Nov2026.
methodology.requirementCoding: Explicit numeric, degree, eligibility, essential, and logistics statements are separated from general listed expectations and sections marked Preferred, Nice to Have, Bonus, or Ideally. These summaries do not replace the actual employer wording.
methodology.futureLimit: Current descriptions show examples of work and eligibility. They do not establish future demand or that a specific framework will remain valuable.
methodology.copyright: Captured employer material remains third-party content. The user-facing report should quote briefly, summarize analytically, and link the original role URLs rather than redistribute full job descriptions.
methodology.sourceQuality: H17 contains unfinished templates and is excluded from sponsorship/remote eligibility conclusions. H18 has a separate unqualified no-sponsorship statement without the H17 template block.
